name: OET-style Nursing Speaking Role-play
description: Evaluates a nurse in a five-minute OET-style role-play with a patient, relative, or carer, using the structure of the published OET Speaking criteria: four linguistic criteria (0-6) and five clinical communication criteria (0-3). This is a practice estimate, not an official OET result.

anchors.6 / 90-100: Speech flows at a natural rate; hesitation only while choosing what to say, never while searching for words.
anchors.5 / 75-85: Minor hesitation or repetition that does not strain the listener.
anchors.4 / 60-70: Noticeable pauses, false starts, or self-corrections, but the message keeps moving.
anchors.3 / 45-55: Frequent pausing and reformulation; the listener has to wait for meaning.
anchors.0-2 / 10-40: Fragmented, slow speech that repeatedly breaks down.

anchors.6 / 90-100: Wide range of accurate structures and vocabulary used flexibly to explain, reassure, and negotiate.
anchors.5 / 75-85: Good range with occasional errors that never obscure meaning.
anchors.4 / 60-70: Adequate range for the task; errors are noticeable but meaning stays clear.
anchors.3 / 45-55: Limited range; errors sometimes make the listener work to follow.
anchors.0-2 / 10-40: Very limited range; errors often block meaning.

anchors.3 / 85-100: Opens appropriately, stays respectful and non-judgmental, shows empathy in words, explores the patient's ideas, concerns and expectations, and picks up their cues.
anchors.2 / 60-80: Warm and respectful, but explores the patient's perspective only partly or responds to cues late.
anchors.1 / 30-55: Polite but task-focused; concerns are noticed but not explored, or empathy is formulaic.
anchors.0 / 0-25: Dismissive, judgmental, or ignores the patient's stated concern.

anchors.3 / 85-100: Sequences the conversation logically, signposts topic changes, moves from open to closed questions, avoids compound or leading questions, and summarises.
anchors.2 / 60-80: Generally organised, with some abrupt topic changes or a compound question.
anchors.1 / 30-55: Loosely organised; questions are mostly closed or leading.
anchors.0 / 0-25: No discernible structure; the patient cannot tell where the conversation is going.

anchors.90-100: Finds out what the patient already knows, gives information in small chunks in lay language, pauses, checks understanding, and the information is accurate and safe.
anchors.70-80: Accurate, mostly lay language; understanding checked once or chunking uneven.
anchors.50-60: Some jargon left unexplained or information delivered in a long block.
anchors.30-40: Frequent jargon, or information incomplete for the task.
anchors.10-20: Inaccurate or unsafe information, or the patient is left unable to act on it.

checklist.item: Greeted the patient/relative, introduced self and role, and confirmed who they are
Found out what the patient/relative already knows or is worried about before explaining
Acknowledged the patient's/relative's concern or emotion explicitly
Covered every task on the role-play card
Explained in lay language, in small chunks, without unexplained jargon
Checked understanding (teach-back or an open check), not just 'Do you understand?'
Signposted and closed the conversation with a brief summary and next step
